question: For the same 70,000-row run-owned native Sheet whose XLSX export exceeded 10 MiB, can files.download also materialize PDF and ODS within bounds suitable for Cirrove’s current all-formats-on-open package path?
kind: Pre-registered direct read-only two-format probe; no cloud mutation.
source_item: The exact run-owned Sheet recorded privately by google-native-lro-large-20260922; no other item is selected.
arms: A: verify exact ID, parent, selected Shared Drive and source version
B: run one bounded LRO PDF request with at most 10 polls and a 64 MiB response bound; inspect PDF signature without logging content
C: run one bounded LRO ODS request with the same bound; inspect ZIP integrity and ODS mimetype; verify source version unchanged
endpoint: Record each format’s success, size, polling and latency independently. This probe passes the current package-materialization feasibility gate only if both complete within 32 MiB and within the 60-second directory deadline together; otherwise leave implementation scoped and document the limitation.
prediction: ODS should be comparable to XLSX. A 70,000-row PDF may be much larger or slower and may exceed the current all-formats-on-open bounds.
limits: One artificial Sheet; no mounted Cirrove read or arbitrary format fidelity. No change to source bytes.

result.interpretation: Both direct exports were valid but together took about 192 seconds; the PDF alone exceeded the service’s 60-second package directory deadline and a 32 MiB artifact cap. The source version changed across this read-only probe, perhaps delayed import settling, but cause is unclassified. The current all-formats-on-open package design cannot simply switch to LRO and claim large-sheet support.

followup_question: After the slow read-only export run, do two exact metadata GETs 30 seconds apart report a stable source version for the run-owned Sheet?
followup_endpoint: Record whether the version is stable; this diagnoses timing but does not erase the original failed feasibility endpoint or prove the cause of the earlier change.

followup_result.interpretation: The fixture settled by this follow-up, but the earlier version change remains real and unclassified.
